facts.fact: 她的鬼理论开篇：别以为他们留在生前的地盘——他们像我们：有时卡在旧辙，有时令自己吃惊。
facts.anchor: You’d think the rule would be that they stayed where they belonged, like their haunts when they were alive would be the same as when they were dead. But it isn’t like that. They’re like us. Sometimes they’re stuck in a rut, sometimes they surprise themselves.

facts.fact: 他们喜欢曼哈顿因为它是岛（水善于划界）；她在 Coney、Rockaways 的海浪里也见过鬼——「你以为他们像空气，其实他们像水，而且一样情绪化」。
facts.anchor: They like Manhattan because Manhattan is an island, and water does a good job of creating a boundary. I’ve seen ghosts in the surf, too, at Coney, the Rockaways. You’d think they’re like air, but really they’re like water, and just as emotional.

facts.fact: 游行现场到处是鬼，人人能看见（哪怕不知看的是什么）——「街上挤满鬼、挤满人，我甚至分不出区别」。（队伍里有里根扮玛丽·安托瓦内特的 Let Them Eat Cake 花车、TWA 空姐装的皇后们——手包拼出 TWAT。）
facts.anchor: When we got to the parade, the ghosts were everywhere, and everyone could see them, even if they didn’t know what they were looking at. The street was packed with ghosts, with people, I couldn’t even tell the difference.

facts.fact: 官方活动早该结束，游行仍在继续，比开场更 gay 更放肆；「游行仿佛无尽，整座城市——过去与未来——都涌进村」。
facts.anchor: The official event must have ended hours ago, but the parade was still going, a little gayer and more reckless than it must have been at kickoff. The parade felt endless, and the whole city, past and future, was streaming into the Village.

facts.fact: 天使与恶魔母女让她想起第一个万圣节：母亲给她穿红衣、做毡尾巴与角（那张照片跟着他们每次搬家挂在冰箱上）；她希望母亲能看见这场游行，不知她是否看过——她在 Westbeth 有朋友。
facts.anchor: I saw a mother and daughter dressed as an angel and a devil, and I remembered—or maybe I just recalled the picture that hung on our fridge from apartment to apartment—my first Halloween, where my mother dressed me in red and made me a felt tail and horns.

facts.fact: 「像所有人都能感觉到——这世界有多满。这种『所有人』的感觉。」
facts.anchor: It felt like everyone could feel it, how full the world was. This sense of everyone.

facts.fact: 高处有个纱布裹成的人形像舞龙般飘过；看不出谁在举她——分不清谁是血肉、谁是记忆与渴望。
facts.anchor: Above all of it was a shrouded figure made of gauze, sweeping through the air like a dragon in a Chinese New Year parade. I tried to see if there were people holding her up, or if, like the dragon, they were in the shroud itself, making it dance, but I couldn’t tell. You couldn’t tell who was muscle and blood and who was memory and want.

facts.fact: 她想：快乐太多了，城市不可能让这种无缰的欢庆长久；可那一瞬她不再觉得城市所有问题是盖顶的油章鱼，而是重新玩了起来——那份快乐与痛一样真实。
facts.anchor: It was too much joy, I thought—there was no way the city would let such unbridled fun go on like this forever. But for a moment, instead of feeling like all the city’s problems were one oily octopus spreading over us and blocking out the sun, I snapped back to having fun, which was just as real as pain.

facts.fact: 一群性别各异的麦当娜身着十字架与黑蕾丝经过，一台音箱放着《Lucky Star》——她以为 Star 会从轮椅里站起来跳舞（那是她的歌），可 Star 只是尽力微笑，感到自己也在其中。
facts.anchor: For a second, I thought Star might get up from her wheelchair and dance—it was her song—but she just smiled the best she could, feeling part of it all.

facts.fact: Claude 要趁 Star 状态好送她回去；她说：「你下班后来我家。过夜。」（Claude 再吻她，她全身涌向她。）
facts.anchor: “When you get off, come to my place,” I said. “Sleep over.”

facts.fact: Bianca 说护送她们回去、把 Star 安顿好；她道别，然后独自在人潮里——朋友们在别处；她会找到他们。
facts.anchor: And then I was alone in the crowd. My friends were somewhere. I’d find them.

facts.fact: 她泪涌：太想他了。不是「他们的歌」，只是他们一起跳过的歌——也许正是这份随意、这次不再用力、不再在心里乞求，才让她看见——
facts.anchor: I missed him so much. It wasn’t our song, it was just a song that we had danced to, and maybe it was that casualness, that moment when I wasn’t forcing it, wasn’t begging in my heart, that I saw—

facts.fact: 「是我们」：他戴那顶像库斯托的针织帽（去年在酒吧被顺走前他最爱的那顶），她穿他的牛仔夹克；她踮脚看游行，他双手扶住她的腰，她跳起来，他托住她一会儿——她在看三年前的我们看游行。
facts.anchor: It was us. He wore the knit hat he used to love before it got swiped in a bar last year, the one that made him look like Jacques Cousteau, and I was wearing his denim jacket. I was standing on my tiptoes to see the parade and he put his hands on my waist and I leapt up and he held me there for a moment.

facts.fact: 她掐自己的手臂确认能感到痛（她没死、不是看自己的鬼）；不是他的鬼，是他们两个过去的自己——「那感觉是自由。我感到他自由了。」即便看不见，她也觉得所有人都在。
facts.anchor: It wasn’t like seeing Patrick or François or anyone I had loved and lost and tried to hold on to. It felt free. I felt that he was free.

facts.fact: 「也许是因为此前那份释放感——但这次我知道：那一夜掀起的过去那层永远会为我、为任何知道怎么看的人留着。」她可以永远看着我们，但不能要求更多，即便那还不够。
facts.anchor: Maybe it was the feeling of release from before, but I knew this time that the layer of the past that the night had kicked up would always be there for me, for anyone, if they knew how to look.

facts.fact: 「我能拥有的他，永远只有我们已经拥有的那些。那不够——可那么多。」
facts.anchor: All I’d ever have of him is what we already had. It wasn’t enough, but it was so much.

facts.fact: 结尾：「我看着 Mark 牵起我的手，我们消失在人群里。我抓紧了，然后松开了。」
facts.anchor: I watched Mark take me by the hand and we disappeared into the crowd. I held on, and I let go.
